newsitem.title: USA: RTRS-US VIEW: Westfield eyes U.S. buys.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-US VIEW: Westfield eyes U.S. buys.

text.p: Encouraged by the initial success of a massive U.S. expansion drive, Australian shopping centre developer Westfield Holdings Ltd says judicious acquisitions will help its continued growth in North America.

Westfield executive director Peter Lowy told Reuters a reorganisation of the company's vast U.S. interests, including a public share offer through an Australian unit trust listed in July, was proceeding well.

The float raised A$402 million of public money for a 50.9 percent stake in the trust and Westfield indicated that it would attempt to raise further capital through private placement to U.S. and European investors.

The funds are to be used to acquire the 50 percent share not already owned by Westfield and the Lowy family in CenterMark, a U.S. property portfolio which includes ownership of 22 shopping centres throughout America worth an estimated $A2.139 billion.
Lowy said he had "no doubt" the Westfield America Trust (WAT) set up to make the acquisition in CenterMark would meet revenue predictions listed in the WAT prospectus.
He said further Westfield growth would be achieved by redeveloping the existing portfolio and acquiring other U.S. centres.
"We'll look at them but we're not running around looking to buy another 25 centres," said Lowy, who added there were a "a lot" of North American centres on the market.
"If they come up and we have the capital ... then we'll look at doing it. We'll be judicious," he said.
"(But) we're 44 percent leveraged, we're not looking to leverage ourselves up. We just took $400 million out of the Australian market, which was a huge chunk," he said.
Lowy said the size of the float had probably led to initial market nervousness.
However Westfield executives were pleased with the outcome of the offer, with units recently touching $1.07.
Lowy said WAT had already attracted "a Dutch investor and a couple of Americans".
"We'd like to get some more international investment," he said. "But it's a little early."

Westfield has a long history in the United States, first entering the North American market in 1977 and quickly building a strong centre management reputation there with 19 locations under its control by 1980.
The company bought into a huge New Jersey shopping centre development in 1993 and a year later acquired a 40 percent interest in CenterMark.
Lowy said the company has slowly adapted to the U.S. style of shopping centre retailing -- more fashion orientation -- but had added an Australian touch to a number of outlets.
"We have more life and more atmosphere in Australia, with entertainment and things," he said.
"If you look at it we are probably bringing the American centres closer to the Australian centres and the Australian centres a little closer to the American," he said.
The U.S. retail market, which Lowy said was "very strong" for most of the first half of the calendar year, still looked solid despite a tough July.
"We will make what's in prospectus, no doubt," he said.
Westfield's prospectus for WAT forecasts distributable income for the trust of A$71.243 million in calendar 1997, giving an effective 10 percent pre-tax yield.
"Next year's looking pretty good; some of the developments we started prior to the IPO will be coming on line," Lowy said.
"I think the American economy will produce a couple years more of what we've had, slow growth and low inflation -- which isn't a bad picture," he said.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
